item.title: Rotting food waste emits 5 times more greenhouse gases than planes
item.description: Rotting food waste is causing up to 10 per cent of total global greenhouse gas emissions – five times more than the entire aviation sector, the UN’s environment agency warned this week.

item.title: Uganda’s UN-supported wildlife forensics lab turns ivory seizures into convictions
item.description: The package originated in Entebbe, Uganda, bound for Cairo, containing 10 kilograms of thumb-sized pieces that could have been either bone or elephant ivory.

item.title: ‘Money alone won’t get us there’: UN steps up aid for 12 forgotten crises
item.description: Getting aid to people in the world’s most neglected emergencies takes more than money. It takes open roads, open borders and leaders willing to help it reach those in dire need.

item.title: Global life expectancy bounces back to near pre-pandemic levels, WHO says
item.description: People around the world are living longer again, with global life expectancy almost fully recovered from the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

item.title: Ukraine war ‘a human rights catastrophe’ that must end, says Türk
item.description: The war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe that is “growing and intensifying by the week” and threatening an even greater disaster across the region, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Friday.

item.title: Collective action needed to tackle global information crisis, UN-led dialogue hears
item.description: Governments, UN entities, civil society, media, academia and the private sector have called for stronger cooperation and practical action to respond to a rapidly changing global information landscape.

item.title: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
item.description: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence as it continues to “adapt and expand”, the UN’s top rights official, Volker Türk, said on Friday.

item.title: Escalating fighting in Yemen deepens food security crisis
item.description: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger that could have consequences in the wider region and beyond, the World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday.

item.title: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
item.description: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

item.title: ‘I have not lost my dreams’: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions
item.description: A teenage girl who fled war-torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn.

item.title: UN Member States weigh latest Security Council veto, this time on Iran
item.description: The General Assembly met on Thursday to examine the Security Council’s latest veto, cast by China and Russia over a United States-backed sanctions panel of experts on Iran nuclear facilities.

item.title: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief
item.description: The UN human rights chief and nine independent rights experts on Thursday called on authorities in Tennessee not to pursue any further attempts to execute Christa Pike, saying her case highlights multiple concerns surrounding the death penalty.

item.title: ‘Women are not victims’: Türk calls for women to be at the heart of peace and security
item.description: Women must be at the centre of efforts to prevent conflict and build lasting peace, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Thursday.

item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday.

item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province.

item.title: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life’, says top Middle East peace envoy
item.description: The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.

item.title: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion
item.description: Artificial Intelligence or AI – and the technology behind it – is moving fast. The question being asked across the world is who gets a seat at the table deciding how it's used and who gets to benefit.

item.description: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday.

item.title: Somali families face renewed violence amid worsening hunger crisis

item.title: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
item.description: Homicide rates are falling across much of the world, but organised crime is on the rise in many regions as criminal networks diversify into trafficking, migrant smuggling, and the exploitation of natural resources, a new UN report launched on Wednesday revealed.

item.title: Malaysia: UN agency urges safeguards after refugees returned to Myanmar
item.description: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.

item.title: Lebanon: One in five children goes to bed hungry, says UNICEF
item.description: Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities today, with children increasingly going without food, missing school and being pushed into work as conflict compounds years of economic crisis. "I wanted to buy clothes for my children, but I could not. I also wanted to enrol them in school, but I could not afford that either," said one father of four, cited on Wednesday by the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Deadly Myanmar strikes as Malaysia begins deportations, new emergency funding released, Gaza and West Bank update
item.description: The UN chief on Tuesday strongly condemned an airstrike that reportedly killed at least 50 people at a market in Myanmar’s Rakhine state and called for those responsible to be held to account.

item.title: Funding cuts put 8.3 million refugees at risk of losing vital assistance
item.description: Haji Mohammad Shafi spent 44 years in Pakistan before he was forced to leave. He sold everything he owned and returned to Afghanistan with his five children, arriving with almost nothing.

item.title: LIVE: Weighing nuclear risks amid rising tensions and war
item.description: Amid rising tensions, extreme weather impacts and strikes on nuclear infrastructure in war-torn Iran and Ukraine, UN Member States returned to the core issue of disarmament on Tuesday, closing out the General Assembly’s High-Level Week with calls for greater safeguards.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
item.description: The Security Council met in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east, despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors focused on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record, which has killed more than 3,900 people.

item.title: DRC: Early access to care and oxygen decisive for Ebola patients’ survival – WHO
item.description: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health workers fighting the country’s largest-ever Ebola outbreak are struggling to overcome critical challenges to patient care, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday.
